statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and no NQ price path exists to score, while Stress rises to 60 on an unattributed Aramco refinery fire in Riyadh, reported Saudi preparations for an operation near Bab al-Mandeb, and a 10-year Treasury yield at 5.28%.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band for every hour of this window, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON and green throughout. All 24 scored hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt; the restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about five hours beyond the final scored hour, so restart gap risk is not scored in this publication. The Gulf equity session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October is the only interval containing an open venue able to respond to the refinery incident, and under the delayed-evidence rule it informs Stress and Confidence rather than current Nasdaq-100 structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this publication.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 while an unattributed Riyadh refinery fire and reported Saudi strike preparations lift Stress to 60
body: Friday 2 October remains the last traded session before the halt. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, after a soft September employment report showed payroll growth missing expectations, unemployment ticking up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings up only 0.1% on the month against about 0.3% expected, with annual wage growth slowing to 3.0% from 3.2%. The structurally decisive detail for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced into a close near the 30,737.07 session low. That is orderly mean reversion, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3 across the whole window. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39, with a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt rather than stress acceleration. Stress is 60 and drifts to 66 across the window on the carried-in environment rather than on observed structure. Treasury yields reversed upward despite the soft print: the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%, and Friday's close is reported at 4.84% on the 2-year and 5.28% on the 10-year after an intraday 5.34% high described as the strongest since 2002. Brent settled at $102.25, down 0.06% on the day but up 7.05% on the month and 58.45% on the year, with Trading Economics attributing Friday's level to additional reported U.S. military deployments to the Middle East and China's decision to halt fuel exports this month. Equity breadth stayed narrow, with AI and semiconductor leadership carrying the index while higher rates weighed on cyclicals; narrow leadership is a Stress and Confidence input and does not mechanically raise Tail. The dominant new input since the previous publication is geopolitical. Reuters-sourced reporting describes a large plume of smoke and flames near Aramco's Riyadh refinery, an asset of roughly 130,000 barrels a day, from Saturday morning; NASA FIRMS VIIRS thermal detections and satellite imagery indicate a large fire with probable emergency flaring and at least three storage tanks showing visible signs of fire. As of this assessment neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco had confirmed the incident or its cause, no group had claimed responsibility, and no damage, casualties or production impact had been reported. Separately, Axios reporting citing two U.S. officials describes Saudi Arabia preparing a major operation against the Houthis in coming days targeting coastal areas near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, with the Saudi defence minister having briefed the U.S. defence secretary and a U.S. official saying Washington is not taking kinetic action for now. That is a credible unresolved escalation mechanism, but under this framework an unresolved mechanism with no venue able to price it raises Stress and gap risk, not Tail, because Tail requires an observed pathological price path. Confidence is 84: the index level, session range and close, volatility, the H.15 curve, Brent and the seven-day U.S. calendar were each verified from primary or authoritative current sources, and the single material open item is the unexplained Riyadh fire. The shared Finviz context file carried a generatedAt of 29 September and a partial collection status, so it was 90-plus hours stale and was discarded; this assessment rests entirely on independent research. No Nasdaq-100 futures or CFD price discovery is available anywhere inside this forecast window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens in Friday's post-payroll U.S. session with Tail 21-22 and Stress 76-79 under a mixed mode, then decays steadily after the 21:00Z futures close: Tail falls from 14 to 3 and Stress from 74 to 52 across the overnight and Saturday hours, with the mode settling to normal from 00:00Z. The last six hours sit flat at Tail 3 while Stress troughs at 52 and recovers to 58 as the Gulf energy thread reopened.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this forecast window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no NQ price path can form and Tail is held flat at 3, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 60 to 66 because the unattributed Riyadh refinery fire, reported Saudi preparations for an operation near Bab al-Mandeb and a 5.28% 10-year accumulate without a venue able to price them. Confidence eases from 84 to 78 as Friday's verified levels age. The one genuinely differentiating interval is the Gulf equity session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October, the only open market relevant to the refinery incident; under the delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure. The CME restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about five hours past the final scored hour, so the first genuine post-weekend price-path evidence, and any restart gap, falls outside this horizon.
